domain_symbols.geometric_space: projective, affine, metric, and topological spaces

rules.name: Projective incidence seed
rules.input_form: affine incidence data under projective completion
preconditions: A projective-completion model is fixed
rules.operation: Extend affine incidence by adding points at infinity in projective geometry.
examples: Parallel affine lines meet at a projective point at infinity after projective completion
counterexamples: Keeping Euclidean parallel nonintersection unchanged in projective completion is invalid

rules.name: Affine combination seed
rules.input_form: weighted point combination with coefficients summing to 1
preconditions: The coefficient field and affine space are fixed
rules.operation: Construct affine combinations independently of a chosen origin.
examples: Line segments and affine spans are described by affine rather than purely linear combinations
counterexamples: Arbitrary coefficient sums define linear combinations, not affine ones in general

rules.name: Hyperbolic parallel seed
rules.input_form: point and line in hyperbolic geometry
rules.output_form: multiple nonintersecting lines through the point
preconditions: A standard hyperbolic model is fixed
rules.operation: Use hyperbolic parallel behavior in place of Euclidean uniqueness.
examples: Hyperbolic parallel behavior differs fundamentally from Euclidean uniqueness of parallels
counterexamples: Imposing Euclidean parallel uniqueness inside hyperbolic geometry is invalid

rules.name: Convex hull seed
rules.input_form: subset of an affine space
preconditions: A convexity notion in an affine or vector space is fixed
rules.operation: Build the convex hull as the minimal convex enclosure.
examples: Finite point clouds generate polygons or polyhedra through convex hull construction
counterexamples: Arbitrary enclosing nonconvex sets do not define the convex hull

rules.name: Triangulation seed
rules.input_form: object decomposed into simplices
preconditions: Face-gluing compatibility is fixed
rules.operation: Decompose an object into simplices with compatible face structure.
examples: Discrete geometry and topology often reduce global structure to simplicial pieces
counterexamples: Overlapping simplices with inconsistent face data are invalid as a triangulation

rules.name: Knot equivalence seed
rules.input_form: pair of embedded circles in three-space
preconditions: Embeddings are taken in the standard knot-theoretic category
rules.operation: Classify knots by ambient isotopy.
examples: Knot type is preserved by continuous deformation that avoids cutting and self-intersection passage
counterexamples: Arbitrary planar diagram similarity does not determine knot equivalence

rules.name: Symplectic form seed
rules.input_form: differential 2-form on a manifold
rules.output_form: symplectic structure when closed and nondegenerate
preconditions: An even-dimensional smooth manifold and differential-form structure are fixed
rules.operation: Recognize a symplectic structure by closedness and nondegeneracy of a 2-form.
examples: Hamiltonian phase spaces carry geometry through closed nondegenerate 2-forms
counterexamples: A degenerate 2-form is not symplectic

rules.name: Homeomorphism-type invariant seed
rules.input_form: geometric or topological object with candidate invariant
preconditions: An active category of homeomorphism or isotopy equivalence is fixed
rules.operation: Require invariants to survive the appropriate topological equivalence relation.
examples: Manifold and knot classification questions are phrased in terms of homeomorphism-type or isotopy invariants
counterexamples: Metric quantities alone are not automatically topological invariants

rules.name: Cross-ratio seed
rules.input_form: ordered quadruple of collinear projective points
preconditions: A projective line model and admissible quadruple are fixed
rules.operation: Use cross-ratio as a projective invariant of four collinear points.
examples: Projective structure retains cross-ratio information even when affine distances are not preserved
counterexamples: Arbitrary metric ratios of segments are not projective invariants in general

rules.name: Projective duality seed
rules.input_form: projective incidence statement
preconditions: A projective duality correspondence is fixed
rules.operation: Swap point and line roles through projective duality.
examples: Incidence theorems often generate dual companions by swapping points with lines in the projective plane
counterexamples: Euclidean metric claims do not automatically survive projective dualization

rules.name: Affine transformation seed
rules.input_form: map on an affine space with linear-plus-translation structure
preconditions: An affine space and affine transformation law are fixed
rules.operation: Preserve affine combinations, lines, and parallelism through affine transformations.
examples: Barycentric structure survives translations and linear distortions even when Euclidean lengths do not
counterexamples: Arbitrary nonlinear maps are not affine transformations

rules.name: Geodesic model seed
rules.input_form: curved geometric model with candidate shortest paths
preconditions: A non-Euclidean model and geodesic notion are fixed
rules.operation: Use model-dependent geodesics in place of Euclidean straight lines.
examples: Straight lines in Euclidean space are replaced by model geodesics in hyperbolic and spherical geometry
counterexamples: Forcing Euclidean straightness into curved models is invalid

rules.name: Helly-type seed
rules.input_form: finite family of convex sets
preconditions: A convex family in a standard affine space is fixed
rules.operation: Infer global intersection structure from small convex subfamilies.
examples: Global intersection of many convex sets can be certified from small subfamilies rather than exhaustive checking
counterexamples: Arbitrary nonconvex families do not automatically satisfy Helly-type conclusions

rules.name: Polytope face seed
rules.input_form: polytope with candidate face-incidence structure
preconditions: A polytope and incidence interpretation are fixed
rules.operation: Organize polytope structure through its hierarchy of faces.
examples: Combinatorial face lattices encode much of a polytope's discrete structure beyond one visualization alone
counterexamples: A generic point set is not automatically a polytope with consistent face data

rules.name: Reidemeister move seed
rules.input_form: pair of knot diagrams
preconditions: A standard knot-diagram setting is fixed
rules.operation: Recognize knot equivalence through sequences of Reidemeister moves.
examples: Local diagram changes can preserve ambient-isotopy class without cutting the knot
counterexamples: Arbitrary redrawing that changes crossing structure is not automatically knot-equivalent

rules.name: Symplectic capacity seed
rules.input_form: symplectic manifold with candidate embedding constraint
preconditions: A symplectic structure and capacity setting are fixed
rules.operation: Use symplectic capacities to constrain embeddings beyond volume data.
examples: Symplectic geometry can distinguish embedding possibilities invisible to mere volume comparison
counterexamples: Volume preservation alone does not determine symplectic embeddability

rules.name: Surgery seed
rules.input_form: manifold or knot-complement modification data
preconditions: A controlled cut-and-glue topology construction is fixed
rules.operation: Modify topological objects through compatible surgery constructions.
examples: New topological objects can be produced by local replacement rules that alter global classification data
counterexamples: Arbitrary cutting and regluing with no compatibility data is invalid as surgery

rules.name: Canonical form normalization expansion
rules.input_form: raw expression E
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Rewrite expressions into a canonical form that preserves the active equivalence relation.
examples: x + y and y + x map to a shared canonical additive form in commutative settings
counterexamples: Applying canonicalization rules outside their preconditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Substitution soundness expansion
rules.input_form: expression F(x) with admissible substitution x <- g
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Substitute only under explicit domain and structural admissibility constraints.
examples: Replacing a variable by a constrained expression must preserve declared domain assumptions
counterexamples: Substitution that violates assumptions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Composition rule expansion
rules.input_form: objects A and B with a valid composition law
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Compose structured objects when composition preconditions are satisfied.
examples: Function and operator compositions require compatible codomain-domain interfaces
counterexamples: Composing incompatible objects is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Inverse admissibility expansion
rules.input_form: object A with invertibility conditions
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Introduce inverses only when invertibility conditions are explicitly satisfied.
examples: Matrix inversion requires nonsingularity
counterexamples: Assuming inverses exist without conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Constraint propagation expansion
rules.input_form: state with constraints C and transform T
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Propagate constraints through each accepted transformation step.
examples: Positivity or boundedness constraints should be preserved or updated after transformation
counterexamples: Dropping constraints silently is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Boundary condition integration expansion
rules.input_form: model equation with boundary or endpoint constraints
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Include boundary and endpoint constraints in the active model state before solving.
examples: Differential models require boundary or initial data to identify admissible solution families
counterexamples: Solving while ignoring required boundary conditions is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Conservation tracking expansion
rules.input_form: model evolution with candidate conserved quantity Q
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Track whether declared conserved quantities remain invariant under model evolution.
examples: Energy-like quantities can be validated as conserved under symmetry assumptions
counterexamples: Declaring conservation without validation is invalid
common_errors: Using auto-generated rules without confirming domain-specific assumptions

rules.name: Approximation error budget expansion
rules.input_form: approximation method and tolerance epsilon
preconditions: Auto-expansion rule requires explicit domain assumptions and validation metadata
rules.operation: Attach explicit error bounds or estimates to approximation-driven outputs.
examples: Numerical approximations should report residual or tolerance-constrained error
